body:
Global crypto markets are nursing a bruising session on November 3, 2026, with total market capitalization sitting at $2.62T after shedding 3.16% over the past 24 hours. Volume of $69.3B tells you this is not a low-conviction drift lower — there is genuine selling pressure here. The Fear and Greed index collapsed to 26 today from 37 yesterday, a move that in one session wiped out what little composure the market had left, and BTC dominance holding at 59.2% confirms that capital is consolidating into the perceived safety of the largest asset rather than rotating into risk. The mood is defensive, the bids are thin, and outside of a handful of idiosyncratic names, there is no compelling evidence that buyers are stepping in front of this.

Bitcoin trades at $77,205, down 0.70% over 24 hours and off 3.63% on the week, with only a faint hourly uptick of 0.05% offering any near-term comfort. The 7-day trend is the more meaningful signal — this is a sustained grind lower, not a flash washout. At $28.1B in daily volume, liquidity is present but not dominant, which means the path of least resistance remains south absent a catalyst. The $77,000 handle is now the line in the sand on a closing basis; a clean break below it on volume re-opens a conversation about the mid-$70,000 range. On the upside, recapturing $79,000 with conviction would be the first sign that the weekly bleeding is slowing. CoinDesk noted Bitcoin is breaking a midterm election pattern going back to 2014 — that historical anomaly is worth flagging as a sentiment variable even if it is not yet directionally tradable.

Ethereum at $2,284.8 is holding up comparatively well, off just 0.09% in the last 24 hours against Bitcoin's steeper 0.70% decline, and the 7-day drawdown of 1.98% is materially shallower than most of the field. That relative resilience is notable given ETH dominance at 10.6% — it is not gaining share, but it is not bleeding it either. The divergence stories today belong to 2 names on opposite ends of the ledger. UNI is the standout on the session, up 1.54% over 24 hours and 3.73% on the week, which in this environment amounts to a significant outperformance. XRP adds 1.86% on the day with $1.68B in volume, showing real participation. On the other side, SOL is the most damaged liquid name in the book, down 0.98% today and 7.53% on the week at $93.31, with ADA flat at $0.190362 but surrendering 7.01% over 7 days. BNB's 24-hour decline of 0.92% and weekly loss of 5.95% to $697.32 is not occurring in a vacuum, and the macro context behind that specific move is impossible to ignore.

The dominant macro narrative today is the Binance situation, and it is messy. CZ publicly warned of increasing AI-driven hacks following what headlines describe as Binance's historic $6.4 billion heist, net outflows reportedly reached $5.3 billion before inflows reportedly turned positive at $2.3B. South Korea simultaneously disclosed it has asked its biggest banks to stress-test against a major crypto hack scenario, which is the kind of regulatory reflex that signals systemic concern rather than isolated incident management. Layered on top of this is U.S. midterm election day, with Cointelegraph asking directly what is at stake for crypto in the 2026 vote — regulatory posture on digital assets, capital gains treatment, and stablecoin legislation are all live legislative questions whose trajectory hinges on tonight's results. The Moscow Exchange announcing Bitcoin, Ether, and USDT trading launch in December adds a geopolitical dimension: institutional adoption is accelerating even in jurisdictions under Western sanction regimes, which complicates the regulatory narrative for U.S. policymakers.

Tomorrow's picture hinges almost entirely on 2 variables: the U.S. midterm results and the evolving Binance contagion story. A congressional outcome favorable to crypto-friendly candidates could flip sentiment hard and fast given how deeply oversold the Fear and Greed reading is at 26 — the setup for a relief rally exists if the political catalyst lands right. Conversely, a hostile legislative result combined with any fresh negative development out of Binance — whether further outflows, regulatory action, or another security incident — could push BTC through $77,000 and accelerate the weekly trend into something more structurally damaging. The NEAR token's 7% decline following a token issuance cut proposal passing is a reminder that governance events carry real price risk in altcoins right now. Watch BNB specifically for stabilization signals; if net inflows genuinely hold positive as reported, that is a near-term floor catalyst. Watch UNI and XRP for whether their outperformance is sticky or simply noise in an otherwise deteriorating tape.
